channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: European Central Bank: September hike risk builds – ING
item.description: ING’s Michiel Tukker expects the European Central Bank (ECB) to keep the deposit rate at 2.25% at the upcoming meeting, with a September hike seen as likely as Oil prices rise and markets already price in around 23bp.

item.title: Swiss Franc weakens as safe-haven demand lifts US Dollar
item.description: USD/CHF extends its gains for the fourth successive day, trading around 0.8150 during the European hours on Thursday. The pair appreciates as the US Dollar (USD) gains ground after recovering its daily losses amid rising geopolitical tensions between the United States (US)-and Iran.

item.title: Analysts agree: Hawkish ECB expectations are likely to keep Euro supported
item.description: The Euro (EUR) remains steady above 1.1400 against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday, showing a surprising resilience to the surging Oil prices and the escalation of hostilities in the Middle East.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Energy shock drives weaker currency – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman highlights that rising Oil and natural gas prices are pressuring the Japanese Yen (JPY), with USD/JPY hitting fresh year-to-date highs above 163.00.

item.title: Gold weakens below $4,100 as inflation fears lift Fed hike bets and support USD
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) attracts some sellers during the first half of the European session on Thursday and slides below the $4,100 mark, retreating further from an over two-week high touched the previous day.

item.title: Indian Rupee attracts slight bids on RBI’s provisional support
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) opens marginally higher against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday on possible Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervention in spot and non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) markets to support the currency.

item.title: Gold: Rally capped by rate risks – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ Bart Melek notes that Gold has rebounded on dip buying and short covering after key technical support held, with prices near $4,150/oz.

item.title: Dow Jones futures decline on Middle East tensions, massive AI investment concerns
item.description: Dow Jones futures lose 0.56% to trade around 52,160 during European trading hours on Thursday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq 100 futures decline 0.54% and 0.74%, trading near 7,500 and 28,960, respectively.

item.title: Australian Dollar: RBA tone may turn hawkish – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur highlights a strong Australian labor market, with 76,000 jobs added and participation back near historic highs, prompting markets to raise the implied probability of an RBA hike to 30%.

item.title: US Secretary of State Rubio warns of intensifying military attacks on Iran
item.description: United States (US) Secretary of State Marco Rubio warns that military attacks on Iran could intensify further, as the nation is not ready to make a deal.

item.title: WTI extends rally towards $90 as Middle East energy supply risks intensify
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, extends its winning streak for the fifth trading day on Thursday, is up over 3% at around $88.60 during the European trading session.

item.title: British Pound: Sterling to hand back gains – ING
item.description: ING analysts Chris Turner, Francesco Pesole and James Smith argue Sterling’s summer strength is driven by positioning, carry and possible M&A flows rather than UK fundamentals.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Tests levels sub-0.5800 as bulls run out of steam
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar (NZD) extends losses for the third consecutive day against the US Dollar (USD) on Thursday, with the NZD/USD pair dipping below 0.5800, after being rejected at the 0.5875 area earlier in the week.

item.title: South African Rand: Hawkish SARB could strengthen ZAR – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists expect a 25bp rate hike in South Africa after a sharp June inflation surprise, with Headline Consumer Price Index (CPI) at 5.0% and core at 4.1%.

item.title: Forex Today: Focus shifts to ECB rate call, while tensions remain high in Middle East
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Thursday, July 23:

item.title: Australian Dollar remains steady following improved employment data
item.description: AUD/USD holds ground after registering minor gains in the previous day, trading around 0.7000 during the European hours on Thursday. The pair remains steady as the Australian Dollar (AUD) moves little following the release of improved Australian employment data.

item.title: European Central Bank set to hold interest rates amid cooling inflation and weaker growth
item.description: The European Central Bank (ECB) is expected to hold the interest rate on the main refinancing operations and the deposit facility steady at 2.4% and 2.25%, respectively. The decision will be announced on Thursday at 12:15 GMT.

item.title: Brent: Energy risk premium rises – RaboResearch
item.description: Rabobank strategist Michael Every warns that escalating conflict around Hormuz and the Red Sea could push Brent above its current USD 95.5 level and widen crack spreads further.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Further losses toward 163.50 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note after USD/JPY hit a 40‑year high above 163, now expect intraday consolidation between 162.80 and 163.30 as recent price action offers few fresh clues.

item.title: USD/JPY Price Forecast: Remains above 163.00 near fresh 40-year highs
item.description: USD/JPY inches higher after posting minor losses in the previous day, trading around 163.20 during the European hours on Thursday. The currency pair is holding a clear bullish bias as spot remains above both the nine-day and 50-day Exponential Moving Averages (EMAs).

item.title: Turkish Lira: Dovish corridor risks for TRY – Commerzbank
item.description: Tatha Ghose at Commerzbank expects Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye (CBRT) to leave the 37% repo rate unchanged, while operationally signaling readiness to normalise the corridor and re-enable weekly repo once war risks ease.

item.title: British Pound bulls seem hesitant as intervention fears and hawkish BoJ bets support Yen
item.description: The GBP/JPY cross extends its directionless price moves through the early European session on Thursday, though it holds above the weekly low and currently trades around the 218.15-218.20 region.

item.title: Euro: Hawkish ECB stance to limit downside against US Dollar – ING
item.description: ING’s Francesco Pesole expects the ECB to leave rates unchanged but deliver a hawkish hold, with Middle East tensions and rising European gas prices keeping hawks in control.

item.title: Euro rallies against the Pound as markets brace for ECB's monetary policy decision
item.description: The Euro (EUR) appreciates for the sixth consecutive day against the British Pound on Thursday, with bulls testing last week’s highs at the 0.8645 area. The Sterling remains offered across the board as investors wonder how the new cabinet will fund its spending pledges.

item.title: Equities: Mixed global performance following earnings – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists highlight a mixed performance across global equities over the last 24 hours. United States (US) stocks were softer, with the S&P 500 slightly lower, while Asian indices such as KOSPI, Hang Seng and Nikkei advanced and European equities saw gains led by STOXX 600.

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: Weakens to near 101.00, but retains bullish tone above 100-day SMA
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), an index of the value of the US Dollar (USD) measured against a basket of six world currencies, currently trades near 101.00 in the early European trading hours on Thursday. The DXY weakens amid improved risk sentiment.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Struggles to return above 20-day EMA
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) trades marginally higher to near 1.3387 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Thursday. The GBP/USD pair edges higher as the US Dollar drops despite surging oil prices in the wake of escalating Middle East energy supply risks.

item.title: Oil: Middle East tensions raise supply risks – MUFG
item.description: Lloyd Chan at MUFG underscores escalating US–Iran tensions and threats to energy infrastructure and shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb.

item.title: Silver Price Forecasts: XAG/USD stalls below $60 as US yields rally
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) is trading practically flat, a few cents below the $60.00 level on Thursday, with upside attempts capped as US Treasury yields jump to fresh highs.

item.title: British Pound: Downside risks below 1.3340 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann expect GBP/USD to consolidate intraday between 1.3350 and 1.3400 after a modest pullback from recent lows.
